### The University of Jordan

#### Course Offerings

---

**Course No.** | **Course Title** | **Number of credit hours**
--- | --- | ---
0431333 | Contemporary Intellectual Traditions | 3

**Prerequisite course:** None  
This course aims to introduce the most prominent contemporary intellectual currents and Islam's stance towards them, to familiarize students with the ideas of these intellectual currents: the secular current (national secularism), the atheistic materialist current (communism and Marxism), the anarchist current (existentialism and hippie), the pornographic current (Freudianism, theory Relative morality), the utilitarian materialist current (pragmatism), and globalization, and explaining the effects of these incoming currents on contemporary Islamic thought.  

---

**Course No.** | **Course Title** | **Number of credit hours**
--- | --- | ---
0431312 | Quranic Stories | 3

**Prerequisite course:** None  
The course discusses the concept of the (story) in Qur'an; the characteristics and goals of Qur'anic narratives; methods of research in Qur'anic stories; al- Isra'iliyyat (The accounts narrated by Israelites). The course also concentrates on how the Qur'anic Story assists in understanding the Divine bases of change, in life, soul, and society. An applied discussion is required on some narratives of certain Prophets.

### Eighth: Courses in the Islamic Banking Department (al-Maṣārīf al-Islāmiyyah):

0407101 | The Foundation of Islamic Economics and Finance | 3

**Prerequisite course:** None  
This course deals with the definition of Islamic economics, its sources and characteristics, its comparison with other economic systems, ownership, production, consumption, and the financial system.
